examples.input: `config set retry 5 --reason "no actor env"` with TROUPE_ACTOR not set

results.1:
All six arms: exit 0, prints nothing, and the file now reads:
retry: 5  # attempts
model: opus
The inline comment is kept. No prompt or error appears even though no actor was given.

examples.input: `TROUPE_ACTOR=human:owner config set model sonnet`, then `TROUPE_ACTOR=agent:coder config set retry 7`

results.1:
All six arms: both exit 0 and print nothing. The file now reads:
retry: 7  # attempts
model: sonnet

examples.input: `TROUPE_ACTOR= config set retry 8` (variable set but empty)

results.1: All six arms: exit 2, and the file is unchanged (retry stays 7). Each arm words the error differently, for example `TROUPE_ACTOR: invalid value '': expected human:<id> or agent:<id>` or `troupe: error: TROUPE_ACTOR: '' is not human:<id> or agent:<id>`. An empty value does not fall back to the login name.

All six arms: exit 2 and no history is shown. The error names 'bogus' and says it must be human:<id> or agent:<id>, for example `troupe: invalid TROUPE_ACTOR: 'bogus' (expected human:<id> or agent:<id>)`. Even this read-only command is refused.

context.in_practice: If you leave TROUPE_ACTOR unset, writes just work. If you set it to anything other than human:<id> or agent:<id>, including an empty string, every command stops with exit 2 until you fix it, even reading history. These runs never show which login name was recorded, because the only history command was refused.
context.stakes: Every config change is stamped with who made it. When TROUPE_ACTOR is not set, the name is taken from the login account, so changes work in scripts and CI with no terminal. When TROUPE_ACTOR is set but malformed, the command is refused instead of being stamped with a bad name.
context.tradeoff: Route 1: works with no terminal and no setup, but an unset actor is recorded under the machine's login name rather than a declared human:/agent: identity.

plan_why: Leaving TROUPE_ACTOR unset makes the history actor fall back to the login name (getpass.getuser). The examples compare that with an explicit human actor, an agent actor, an empty TROUPE_ACTOR and a malformed one (which should exit 2).
